about.description3: Whether you're navigating the ancient streets of Cairo, sailing down the Nile, or uncovering Luxor's temple secrets, our platform connects you directly to reliable transport, trusted local guides, and essential attractions—all in just a few clicks.

sinaiGuide.title: Sinai Peninsula Travel Guide
sinaiGuide.subtitle: Your gateway to where ancient history meets the Red Sea's pristine beauty
sinaiGuide.description: Discover the world's most renowned coral reefs, ascend the sacred Mount Sinai at sunrise, and traverse wind-carved dunes alongside Bedouin guides who know every hidden oasis. This is where Moses received the Ten Commandments, where world-class diving meets authentic desert culture, and where budget-conscious travelers find experiences that rival any luxury adventure.

destinations.title: Understanding Sinai's Four Great Destinations
destinations.description: From red-rock canyon landscapes to crystal-clear waters, each destination offers a unique way to experience the Sinai Peninsula's magic.

sharmElSheikh.name: Sharm El Sheikh
sharmElSheikh.description: The Red Sea's crown jewel, evolved from a Bedouin fishing settlement into one of the world's most celebrated diving destinations
sharmElSheikh.details: Perched on the southern tip of Sinai, this resort town offers world-class coral reefs, luxury accommodations, and vibrant nightlife. Experience night-time plankton snorkeling in Nabq Bay where bioluminescent organisms create trails of glowing light.

dahab.name: Dahab
dahab.description: A bohemian coastal town where the name 'gold' reflects both desert sands and sunset hues, beloved by divers and free spirits
dahab.details: Once a modest Bedouin fishing camp, Dahab's laid-back atmosphere attracts adventurers worldwide. The Blue Hole's vertical walls and the Canyon's dramatic drop-offs showcase vibrant marine life, while steady winds make it perfect for windsurfing.

nuweiba.name: Nuweiba
nuweiba.description: A tranquil gateway where ancient trade routes meet pristine coastline, offering authentic Bedouin culture and unspoiled beaches
nuweiba.details: Nuweiba's shores have witnessed millennia of passage from Nabatean caravans to modern travelers. Enjoy sunset Bedouin tea rituals on Aya Bay's dunes and explore the nearby Colored Canyon's sandstone walls glowing in bands of ochre and crimson.

taba.name: Taba
taba.description: The northern gateway of Sinai, where strategic crossroads meet luxury resorts overlooking the Gulf of Aqaba
taba.details: Long serving as the crossroads between Egypt and the Levant, Taba combines historical significance with modern luxury. Elegant cliff-top resorts offer panoramic gulf views while maintaining traditional Bedouin architectural motifs.

bestTime.title: Best Time to Visit
bestTime.content: October to April offers perfect weather (20-25°C). Summer months (May-September) are extremely hot (35-45°C) but great for diving.

gettingThere.title: Getting There
gettingThere.content: Fly into Sharm El Sheikh Airport (SSH) or drive from Cairo (6-7 hours). Taba border crossing connects to Israel/Jordan.

safety.title: Safety Considerations
safety.content: Generally safe for tourists. Stick to established resorts and tour operators. Check current travel advisories for desert areas.

packing.title: What to Pack
packing.content: Reef-safe sunscreen, diving gear (or rent locally), desert clothing, warm layers for mountain treks, comfortable hiking boots.

faq.title: Egypt Travel FAQs
faq.subtitle: Answers to your most common questions—clear, honest, and up-to-date

safety.question: Is Egypt safe for tourists right now?
safety.answer: Yes, Egypt is generally safe for tourists, especially in major destinations like Cairo, Luxor, Aswan, and the Red Sea resorts. We monitor all regions closely and tailor each itinerary to ensure your comfort and safety, with private transport and local support at every step.

visa.question: Do I need a visa to enter Egypt?
visa.answer: Most travelers can obtain an e-Visa online before arrival or purchase one on arrival at major airports. We'll guide you through the process after booking. Some nationalities require pre-approval—check with your local embassy or ask us.

price.question: What's included in my tour price?
price.answer: All our itineraries are fully transparent, with no hidden fees. Inclusions typically cover private transportation, expert guides, entrance tickets, bottled water, and all mentioned activities. Optional extras or personal spending are clearly listed before booking.

customise.question: Can I customise my itinerary?
customise.answer: Absolutely! Our trips are designed around you. Whether you're a couple, a solo traveler, or a family, you can customise everything—hotel category, pace, guides, and even destinations.

currency.question: What currency should I bring?
currency.answer: While Egypt uses the Egyptian Pound (EGP), USD and EUR are widely accepted. We recommend bringing some cash for small purchases and tips, though credit cards are accepted in most hotels and restaurants.

weather.question: What's the best time to visit Egypt?
weather.answer: October to April offers the most comfortable weather with cooler temperatures perfect for sightseeing. Summer (May-September) is hotter but ideal for Red Sea activities and comes with lower accommodation prices.
